paper.title: Structured Scaling of AI Discovery Across Diverse Scientific Domains (SimpleTES)

lede: Where this run stands against what other methods reached on the same problem - the first autocorrelation inequality (lower is better). The reference table comes from arXiv:2604.19341 (SimpleTES), Supplementary Table 17; newer results were added from the community-curated list and the Einstein Arena. For every method whose height sequence is public, the bound is recomputed here from the sequence itself.
league_note: (the table of arXiv:2604.19341 plus the newer Einstein Arena / curated-list results)
league_foot: Values are quoted as printed (lower is better). The paper's own method (SimpleTES, gpt-oss-120b) reaches 1.503871 on AC1 and does not claim the AC1 record - the record in its table is the Together AI entry. Newer replayed results go lower still. Change the Reference selector (top bar) to re-base every gap in this page.
footnote: All numbers are for the discretised problem: a non-negative step function on [−¼, ¼] with n equal steps, score 2n·max(a*a)/(Σa)². Any such score is a valid upper bound for the continuous constant C₁; none of these results says what the true C₁ is.
caution: Entries marked 'claim' come from a preprint listing and a quoted number that I could read but not independently verify. Entries marked 'reported' are taken from the paper / curated list as printed (the curated list says its Oct-2026 rows were independently replayed).

events: Best human bound (Matolcsi-Vinuesa): 1.50973 - the 208-step function is recomputed in the table above.
AlphaEvolve V2 (arXiv:2511.02864) 1319 steps → 1.50316355; ThetaEvolve (arXiv:2511.23473, an 8B model with test-time learning) 1319 steps → 1.50313244.
TTT-Discover (arXiv:2601.16175, the test-time-training method this repo is about): 30,000 steps, printed 1.502870 (exact 1.5028629).
Together AI / Einstein Arena refines the TTT construction: printed 1.502862 - but the construction's exact value is 1.5028628587, i.e. ~9e-7 above the printed figure.
SimpleTES (arXiv:2604.19341): 1.503871 with a 972-step function - the paper says it trails the leading public result.
Einstein Arena paper (arXiv:2606.10402): best arena entry 1.5028609 (prior best 1.5028629).

Einstein Arena leaderboard: AgentDiscover 1.5027435320 (3 Oct, 65,536 heights) and then Atris 1.5027434868 - both independently replayed on the curated 1a page. Much smaller steps than before: ~1.2e-4 below Together AI.

Unreviewed preprint on alphaXiv (3 Nov): three agents certify 1.502664840776 using an exact rational certificate on a 262,144-cell grid; it also quotes MILO's 1.5027435984. No construction release was found, so these two stay claims and are not ranked.
